newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka reforms seen strengthening human rights.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka reforms seen strengthening human rights.

text.p: Sri Lanka's proposed constitutional reforms will strengthen human rights and bring the government closer to the people, Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister G.L. Peiris said on Thursday.

"The aim is to bring government directly within reach of the people," he told a news conference. "The government is to be streamlined so that it can respond more meaningfully and rapidly to the needs of the people."
The reforms offer substantial autonomy to minority Tamils in a bid to end the government's 14-year ethnic war with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.
The proposals, which have been before a parliamentary select committee for about a year, would also see a dramatic expansion of the ambit of human rights, Peiris said.
"There is a world of difference between the old and the new constitutions," he said. "We have recognised a whole range of new rights."
The new constitution would recognise, in explicit terms, the right to life and compel security forces to give reasons when making arrests, he said.

It would also ensure no one could be held for more than 24 hours without being produced before a judicial official, he said. Detainees would be entitled to humane treatment and not depend on the goodwill of the arresting official, he added.

Human rights groups have criticised security forces for human rights abuses in the war against the LTTE, who are fighting for an independent homeland for Tamils in the north and east. The government says it has cracked down on abuses.

The proposed reforms would provide for affirmative action to help disadvantaged sections of society, guarantee the right of privacy and also ensure the right to information which was not recognised in the present constitution, Peiris said.

"It is the government's firm belief that democratic rights cannot be fully enjoyed without the right to information," Peiris said. "You must have complete information at your disposal to be able to criticise government decisions."
Peiris also said an agreement between the government and the main opposition party would help expedite talks on ending the ethnic war.
Peiris was referring to an agreement between President Chandrika Kumaratunga and the United National Party to work together to end the war signed earlier this month.
